This Job Description is not an exhaustive list of all functions that the employee performing this job may be required to perform. Rove Next is a new premium line from Rove Concepts , a Vancouver-based modern furniture brand selling direct to consumer across Canada and the US. Rove Next launches with improved versions of our best-selling pieces, and it needs its own marketing built from the ground up.

That's this role. You'll own how Rove Next reaches customers and keeps them, starting with email and lifecycle. The goal is a marketing function that scales through AI and systems rather than through headcount, and the advantage here is that you're building it clean rather than inheriting one.

This is not a coordination role. We need someone who takes a problem and builds the answer, and who catches things before they reach leadership.

Scope

Initially focused on Rove Next, with room to expand across the Rove Concepts group as the brand grows.

What you'll own

Email and lifecycle as our primary owned channel. Campaign calendar, flows, segmentation, deliverability, list health. We run on Klaviyo.

Quality control on everything that ships. Copy, creative, link destinations, offers, regional versions. If something goes out wrong, it was yours to catch.

Building AI into the daily work. Not proposing it, shipping it.

Working alongside our lifecycle and email team, our designers, and our external ads partner to keep the calendar moving.

Translating results into plain business language. What we spent, what we made, what we'd do differently.

Must-haves

Five or more years in ecommerce or DTC marketing with real ownership of email and lifecycle. Klaviyo or a comparable ESP.

Evidence that you build with AI yourself rather than assigning it. When you hit a wall, your instinct should be to build through it, not to raise a ticket and wait.

Fluent, native-level English, written and spoken. This one is non-negotiable. You will be writing copy that goes out to our customers under our name, so we need someone who can hear the difference between a line that sounds premium and one that sounds like a discount retailer.

A strong eye. You can look at an asset and tell whether the destination matches the promise, whether the tone is right, and whether the offer math actually adds up.

Comfortable being told when something isn't landing, and comfortable telling us the same.

Nice to have

Furniture, home, or another considered-purchase category with a long buying cycle. Shopify, GA4 and Meta Ads familiarity. Experience holding a team to brand guidelines.

What success looks like

Flow revenue grows as a share of total email revenue. Work stops reaching leadership with errors in it. AI is doing measurable work inside the function within 90 days, rather than sitting in a proposal.

Compensation

$3,500 to $4,500 USD per month depending on experience. Independent contractor.

How to apply

Send your CV to []. In a few lines, tell us two things:

One AI workflow or automation you built yourself in a real business. What it did, and what it saved.

One time you caught something before it shipped that nobody else had noticed.

Please also include a short voice note, around 60 seconds, introducing yourself and telling us what you'd want to know before writing your first email for us.

Overview

• At World Business Lenders (WBL), we provide flexible, short-term commercial loans backed by real estate to help small and medium-sized businesses across the United States, particularly those facing difficulties securing traditional financing.

• We are a fast-moving, results-driven organization focused on efficient execution, strong risk management, and protecting the company's collateral position.

About the Role

• The Closing Team Leader supports the day-to-day operations of the Closing function, helping ensure loans move efficiently from Clear-to-Close through funding while meeting quality standards, internal procedures, and required service-level agreements (SLAs).

• This role provides hands-on leadership, guidance, and support to Closing team members, monitors workload and pipeline performance, and helps resolve operational issues that may affect closing timelines or funding. The Closing Team Leader works closely with Title, Underwriting, Credit, Processing, Valuations, Legal, and Funding to ensure closing conditions are satisfied accurately and on time.

• The role also supports coordination with closing attorneys, title companies, settlement agents, and other third-party partners to facilitate timely closings and protect WBL's collateral position.

What Success Looks Like

• Maintain an organized, productive Closing Team with clear priorities and accountability.

• Identify workflow bottlenecks, resolve routine operational issues, and escalate complex exceptions appropriately.

• Support effective coordination across internal departments and external partners while helping protect WBL's collateral position.

postings.title: Senior SDET, Agentic Quality
postings.descriptionText:
About Onfleet

Onfleet ’s mission is to power the future of commerce by enabling businesses of all sizes to move goods more efficiently and delightfully . Our product includes intuitive smartphone apps for drivers, a powerful modern web dashboard for logistics teams, and automatic notifications and real-time tracking for recipients. Onfleet powers millions of deliveries every week for thousands of businesses around the world across a range of industries, from grocery and prepared meals to pharmacy, flowers, and furniture.

About the role

Onfleet is hiring two senior SDETs to shape how our engineering teams build and trust automated quality. At Onfleet , the team that builds a feature owns its quality. Developers write and maintain their own tests. Your job is to make those teams better at it: you pair with them, teach, review, and find the cases they missed. You will not be the person who tests everyone else's work.

Together with our quality leads, you’ll own our test frameworks and the shared quality tooling every team depends on. You’ll also do feature development in production code and internal tooling. You’ll be part of our core quality engineering group, sometimes embedded on one team and sometimes working across several.

You’ll start by taking ownership of our existing automation and making it more reliable and complete, alongside greenfield work on new platform services. We measure this role by what the teams can do because you were there.

How We Work

We code using agents, and nearly 100% of our code is written this way. Generating code is the easy part. Knowing what good looks like, and holding the bar, is the job. The engineers who thrive here are scrutinizing and questioning: they reject AI slop and catch the wrong call before it ships.

Every engineer helps improve how we work instead of only following it. For this role that means building and improving the agentic tooling itself: test generation, review, verification, and the workflows around them.

We are candid and have a low ego. Challenge us on tooling direction, and expect to be challenged back.

What You’ll Do:

•
Strengthen the current suite. Improve reliability, extend coverage, and modernize patterns. A flaky test is a failing test.

•
Own the test frameworks. Unit, integration, and end-to-end, treated with the same care as production code.

•
Own the quality gates in CI/CD (continuous integration and continuous delivery). Pipelines, checks, and gates, so standards are enforced by the system and not by people.

•
Build agentic quality tooling. Extend the agents and workflows we use for test design, review, and verification.

•
Raise the bar through teams. Pair on test design, review code, help make hard-to-reach code testable, and write things down so the practice outlives any one person.

•
Ask the testability question early. In planning, ask how we'll test it and how we'll know it broke in production.

•
Know when a release is healthy. Metrics, dashboards and alerts that tell us something is wrong before a customer does, and that tell a team whether a release is safe to keep rolling out.

•
Ship features. Full-stack work in production code and internal tooling, alongside the teams you support.

What You'll Bring (required):

• 8 or more years of professional software development experience, in any role.

• 5 or more years where building and maintaining test automation was a core part of your job, as an SDET, test automation engineer, or software engineer who owned test infrastructure. Your title matters less than the work.

• You build software, not just tests: test frameworks, internal tools, CI tooling, or product features. You want feature development in production code and internal tooling to be part of your job here.

• Depth across unit, integration, and end-to-end testing, including hands-on work with a browser framework such as Playwright or Cypress.

• Hands-on CI ownership: you have created, configured, or fixed a CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or equivalent), not just used one.

• A track record of being the person who drove automated test coverage on a team, whatever your role was.

• Working knowledge of DevOps practice: how code is built, deployed and monitored in production. You have added metrics, dashboards or alerts so a team knew when something broke.

• Daily professional use of AI coding agents, and experience building or improving agentic tooling, not just using it.

• A multiplier mindset: you get your satisfaction from the team shipping safer and faster, not from your own test count.

• Excellent written and spoken English, roughly C1 level, and experience working day to day on an international team.

Nice To Have:

• Mobile development (Android or iOS) and mobile test automation, using native frameworks such as Espresso or XCUITest, or cross-platform tools such as Appium or Maestro.

• TypeScript, Node.js, and React.

• Rust, or another statically typed language.

• Clear evidence of driving CI/CD practice for a whole team or company.

• Production canaries and progressive delivery: you have used production signals (error rates, latency, business metrics) to decide whether a release continues or rolls back, through canaries, feature flags or automated rollback.

• Test data and environment management: getting a realistic system into a known state quickly and repeatably.

• Test-driven development (TDD).

• AWS and cloud-native services.

Location and Benefits:

• Remote, open to candidates based in Canada or Latin America.

• The team works on US Pacific Time. You'll need to reliably work a schedule that frequently matches US Pacific business hours (9am to 5pm PT).

• Flexible PTO.

• Laptop and work-from-home setup stipend.

• Monthly technology stipends (internet and AI tooling).

Onfleet is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Onfleet 's culture is one that strongly values diversity in its workplace and we are committed to working with potential team members who can bring diverse perspectives and experience to our company and culture.

We do not make hiring or employment decisions on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other basis protected by applicable local, state or federal law.

We highly encourage members of underrepresented groups to apply and we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $70,000 to $95,000 USD per year for candidates in both Canada and Latin America, depending on experience, skills, and background. Where an offer lands within that range reflects the depth and experience a candidate brings to the role.

How We Hire

You need an identity-verified LinkedIn profile to apply. That's the free "Verified" badge, the shield icon next to your name. We check for it, and applications without it don't move forward.

Before any offer, we verify your identity and work history. That includes a live video ID check and reference calls. We use AI, automated systems, and a person to review applications: every application that meets the requirements is also read by an engineering leader or a recruiter. If you misrepresent your identity or experience, the process ends.

postings.title: Senior Performance Creative Editor (Contract)
postings.descriptionText:
Senior Performance Creative Editor (Contract)
Everyday Dose · Remote, Europe or Latin America · $4,000-5,000 USD/month · Contract
We sell mushroom coffee direct to consumers. Paid ads on Meta and Google are how we grow, and the creative is the variable that decides whether it works. We test continuously and we measure what wins, so the feedback you get here is specific rather than taste-based.
Our creative strategists write the scripts and own the angle. You own the execution and, specifically, the first five seconds. You will ship 15 to 25 finished ads a month, deliberately fewer than most performance shops expect, because we would rather you spend the hours deciding what to change than cutting another variant nobody learns from.

What you will do

•
Cut paid ads for Meta and Google from scripts and angles handed to you by a strategist. Vertical, sound-on, short, fast-paced.

•
Own the hook. The script arrives written; the first five seconds are your call. We have firm views, built from our own account data, about which openers work for this product and which quietly kill a good ad. You will learn them in week one, apply them without being asked, and argue when one is wrong.

•
Iterate winners, not only originate. Most of your month is making something that already works work harder, which in our testing beats originating from scratch by a wide margin.

•
Build variants that change one thing on purpose. We have burned whole quarters on same-day copies that duplicated instead of testing. A variant that teaches us nothing is worse than no variant.

•
Read your own numbers. You get access to our creative analytics and attribution tools, and your output is measured. You bring reads to the weekly creative review rather than waiting to be told what lost.

Requirements

What we are looking for
Three or more years cutting ads that ran on a paid account. We care about what you have shipped, not your title.

Required

•
Paid ads as the spine of your work. You can name a brand that spent money distributing something you cut.

•
A performance number you personally moved on a specific piece of creative, before and after.

•
You know which metrics decide and which mislead. An ad is judged on spend and acquisition cost over its first week, not on thumbstop or hold rate. Plenty of good editors optimise for retention and engagement because those are the numbers they are shown. We will ask you which metrics you have actually been held to and what you think they do and do not predict. There is a right answer and it is not the obvious one.

•
AI creation, fluently and invisibly. Generative tooling is how you hit variant volume at this cadence: image and video generation, voice, upscaling, automated captioning and reframing. The bar is output nobody can tell was generated. We are not buying AI-looking content, we are buying your speed.

•
Premiere or DaVinci to a professional standard , plus After Effects or CapCut. You finish your own sound.

• English good enough to argue with a media buyer about why a hook is wrong.

• Your own machine, reliable internet, a quiet place to take a call.

Strongly preferred

• Supplements, wellness, beverage, beauty or DTC subscription. Our claims language is regulated.

• Range across the formats direct response actually runs on: offer-led creative, objection and confession openers, and one person talking to camera. Tell us which you are strongest in.

• Creative analytics tooling such as Motion, Triple Whale or Northbeam.

• Cutting from creator and UGC footage, including the unglamorous work of making mediocre raw material perform.

Not required: a degree, a cinematic showreel, agency names on your resume, or managing anyone. Senior here means judgment, not headcount.

Before you apply
We decline a lot of genuinely skilled editors who have never cut a direct-response ad. That wastes everyone's time, so, plainly:
Not a fit if your portfolio is mainly corporate or internal communications, brand films, weddings and events, news or broadcast, documentary, event recaps and sizzle reels, music videos, real estate, podcast production, long-form YouTube, or B2B training. Those are real crafts and close to the opposite problem: a beautiful 90-second brand film and an ad that holds a stranger for three seconds and sells coffee are not the same skill.
The test: can you name a brand that paid to distribute something you cut, and the metric you were judged on? If the honest answer is that you have made great videos but nobody bought media against them, this seat will not work, and we would rather say so now than after two interviews.
One more thing. A cover letter that repeats this posting back to us reads exactly as it sounds. Tell us about your work instead.

Benefits

Compensation
$3,500-5,000 USD per month, depending on experience and portfolio

Engagement
Independent contractor, ongoing, invoiced monthly.

Location
Remote, anywhere in Europe or Latin America. You are responsible for your own taxes and any local registration.

Hours
Async by default. We ask for 2-3 hours of daily overlap with Austin, Texas (Central Time) for the creative review and buyer conversations. You choose which hours.

Commitment
Full-time equivalent effort. We are not looking for someone fitting this between three other clients.

Equipment
Yours. We provide software seats (Adobe CC, Motion, Frame.io) and all footage, product and creator assets.

You'll join a small, high-leverage Infrastructure team with a clear mandate: multiply what every engineer and agent can do through automation, self-service, and guardrails-by-design. • Build and operate the self-service infrastructure platform. Make the right thing the easy thing, and the secure thing the default.

Within a technical direction set by the team's Staff engineers, build and operate the layers they rely on (a unified CI/CD pipeline, GitOps-based delivery with ArgoCD, an IaC module catalog, and scaffolding for new services), owning specific components end to end. The goal is for engineers and agents to provision infrastructure and ship changes within guardrails, without hand-writing Terraform/Kustomize or waiting on a ticket.

• Make agents first-class developers. Help generalize our agent isolation pattern into reusable platform primitives: sandboxed runtime, workload identity, audit trails, and approval gates. Implement new gates as coverage grows, keep them fast and low-flake, and drive services onto them. Make gate and test results machine-readable and callable outside the PR flow, so agents and humans alike can act on a failure directly.

• Own the reliability and observability of what you build. Create the dashboards and operational controls that make the surfaces you own observable and improvable as throughput grows: gate pass rates, approval-rate and self-service-ratio trends, common failure modes, cost attribution, and DORA metrics surfaced to teams. • Experience building self-service developer platforms, ephemeral environments, CLIs, scaffolding tools, or internal developer portals (Backstage or custom). You treat infrastructure as a product.

postings.title: Director, Data Hall Design, AMERS
postings.descriptionText:
About Nscale

Nscale is the vertically integrated AI cloud engineered for AI. We own and operate the full stack — energy, data centers, GPU superclusters, orchestration, and AI services — delivering high-performance infrastructure to AI-native companies, enterprises, and governments across Europe and the US. We are deploying GPU capacity at hyperscale, operating some of the densest, most advanced AI infrastructure in the world.
At Nscale , our Data Center Design team plays a critical role in turning AI infrastructure requirements into buildable, scalable facilities across our global portfolio. We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscale r, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

About the Role
As Director, Data Hall Design, you will build and lead Nscale 's data hall design practice, the specialist function responsible for the physical design of AI infrastructure inside the data hall. This includes GPU rack layouts, high-speed network and storage topology, structured cabling, fiber tray routing, patch matrices, rack-level power distribution, and bill of materials development.
The role sits at the intersection of AI infrastructure architecture, physical data center design, construction delivery, and operations. You will translate complex GPU, networking, storage, power, and cooling requirements into precise, buildable design packages that construction, installation, procurement, and operations teams can execute with clarity.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role at launch. You will establish standards, templates, and quality processes, and build a scalable team of data hall designers as Nscale 's global portfolio grows.

What You'll be Doing

• Own data hall layout design across Nscale 's AI data center portfolio, from early concept layouts through construction-ready drawing packages.
- Design rack layouts that optimize for GPU cluster topology, compute density, cooling strategy, power distribution, cable management, and operational access.
- Translate network architecture into physical design for spine-leaf, fat-tree, rail-optimized GPU fabric, InfiniBand, Ethernet, storage, and management networks.
- Produce clear data hall design deliverables, including layout plans, rack elevations, cable management plans, fiber tray layouts, patch matrices, topology diagrams, power distribution plans, BOMs, and asset documentation.
- Design structured cabling systems for high-density AI environments, including fiber type, connector type, polarity, bend radius, slack management, labeling, color coding, and documentation standards.
- Integrate thermal and power requirements into data hall layouts, including hot/cold aisle containment, rear-door heat exchangers, direct liquid cooling, immersion cooling, rack loads, power feeds, and cable pathway requirements.
- Develop accurate bills of materials for data hall equipment, cabling, hardware, accessories, and procurement packages, from early budget estimates through construction-ready packages.
- Establish DCIM and asset documentation standards covering rack positions, device assignments, port mappings, power connections, IP addressing, as-built records, and operational handover.
- Partner closely with network engineering, IT architecture, MEP engineering, construction, procurement, operations, commissioning, and design technology teams.
- Develop and maintain reusable data hall design standards, templates, reference layouts, quality review processes, and delivery cadences.
- Stay current on AI hardware evolution, including new GPU generations, switch architectures, optical interconnects, liquid and immersion cooling, and increasing rack power densities.
- Build and lead a team of data hall designers as the portfolio scales, setting expectations for technical quality, documentation, delivery pace, and cross-functional collaboration.

About You

• 10+ years of experience in data hall design, data center infrastructure design, IT infrastructure planning, structured cabling engineering, or a closely related technical field.
- Deep experience designing physical infrastructure for high-density compute environments, including rack layout, power distribution, cooling integration, and structured cabling.
- Strong knowledge of GPU cluster physical design, ideally including NVIDIA DGX/HGX systems, SuperPOD-scale environments, or comparable AI/HPC infrastructure.
- Strong understanding of high-speed networking physical design, including InfiniBand, 100G/400G/800G Ethernet, spine-leaf and fat-tree topologies, and GPU fabric architectures.
- Expertise in structured cabling and fiber infrastructure, including OS2, OM3/OM4/OM5, LC, MPO/MTP, polarity schemes, loss budgets, and high-density fiber management.
- Demonstrated ability to produce production-quality design documentation, including data hall layouts, rack elevations, cable plans, fiber tray layouts, patch matrices, topology diagrams, and BOMs.
- Experience developing procurement-ready bills of materials for complex data hall builds.
- Familiarity with DCIM, IPAM, and asset management platforms such as NetBox, Nlyte, Sunbird, or equivalent systems.
- Proficiency with AutoCAD, Visio, and at least one data center design, BIM, DCIM, or infrastructure documentation tool.
- Working knowledge of rack-level and row-level power distribution, including PDUs, busway, overhead power, and rack power management.
- Experience collaborating with MEP engineers, construction teams, procurement teams, and operations teams in a fast-paced, multi-project environment.
- Ability to set standards, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and turn ambiguous infrastructure requirements into clear, buildable design packages.

Nice to Have

• Experience with direct liquid cooling, rear-door heat exchangers, and immersion cooling integration in high-density data halls.
- Familiarity with NVIDIA NVLink Switch System, Quantum InfiniBand, Spectrum Ethernet, and emerging AI fabric architectures.
- Experience designing AI, HPC, hyperscale, cloud, or mission-critical data center environments.
- Knowledge of optical transceiver types, silicon photonics, co-packaged optics, and their implications for high-speed server and switch connectivity.
- Experience building or leading a data center infrastructure design team.
- Experience integrating data hall assets into BIM, DCIM, digital twin, or operational documentation workflows.
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Network Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.
- Relevant certifications such as BICSI RCDD, BICSI DCDC, NVIDIA DGX-related certifications, Cisco CCNA/CCNP, or equivalent credentials.

Why this role matters
The data hall is where Nscale 's AI infrastructure comes to life. In this role, you will:

• Set a consistent documentation standard across layout, cabling, fiber, patching, rack elevation, power, BOM, and asset documentation for every Nscale data hall.
- Enable GPU clusters to deploy at target density with clean cabling, correct fiber topology, accurate power distribution, and minimal field rework.
- Deliver BOMs that procurement can rely on directly, making missing materials, substitutions, and emergency orders the exception.
- Become a trusted technical partner to network engineering, IT architecture, MEP, construction, and operations from the earliest design stages.
- Make DCIM and as-built documentation complete, current, and trusted as the operational source of truth.
- Grow the data hall design practice from a hands-on lead role into a high-performing team with reusable standards, repeatable processes, and strong delivery discipline.
- Turn Nscale 's data hall designs into a competitive advantage in deploying AI infrastructure quickly, accurately, and reliably.

What We Can Offer You
At Nscale , you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and we want you at the core.

• Highly competitive package, including base salary and equity, with reviews every 12 months.
- Join one of the fastest-growing tech startups: your chance to push boundaries, collaborate with brilliant minds, and make your mark on cutting-edge AI.
- Expect a dynamic progression plan tailored to your ambitions. Grow by trying new things, leading, challenging the status quo, and owning your impact, always with our full support.
- Human-first flexibility. We treat you as humans first. Our flexible workplace trusts Nscale rs to deliver, giving you the autonomy to shape your day around life's moments.
- Join our thriving remote-first team. Geography is no barrier to impact or connection. We build seamless virtual collaboration, empowering you wherever you work.

Equal Opportunities Statement
At Nscale , we are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enrich our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities. We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.
If there's anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

The range below reflects the base salary for the position. Actual compensation may vary based on job-related factors such as skill set, experience, education, and location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus, equity, and/or commission programs. Nscale may offer a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, flexible paid time off, parental leave, and retirement plan participation.

Salary Range

$170,000—$240,000 USD

postings.title: Senior Content Marketer, Campaigns/Enterprise
postings.descriptionText:
About Animalz

Animalz is a content marketing agency that partners with B2B SaaS companies, venture capital firms, and other tech organizations to drive long-term, sustainable growth through high-quality content.
Our fully remote team of experienced content marketers delivers strategies and content tailored to each customer's goals and context. We pride ourselves on our deep interest and understanding of software products and audiences, our commitment to thought leadership, and our relentless pursuit of mastering our craft.
Our customers include industry leaders like Amplitude, Ramp, and Wistia, as well as high-growth early-stage startups.

About the Role
We're looking for a Senior Content Marketer: an exceptional writer with the editorial judgment to own content quality for the customers they serve.
This is a writing-first role. About 70% of your time will be spent researching and writing content yourself—work that calls for real research, original thinking, and craft.
On the Enterprise & Campaigns team, that writing spans various formats: thought leadership that gives leaders a point of view worth repeating, along with the blog posts, guides, landing pages, and email sequences that carry a campaign from first touch to conversion. You'll write for some of our largest customers, whose audiences (and internal reviewers) expect work that holds up under scrutiny.
The rest of your time goes to making sure everything else your accounts publish is just as good as what you write. You'll manage the freelance writers who contribute to your accounts, keep the content calendar on track, review every piece before it reaches the customer, and ensure customer feedback is acted on and remembered.
You won't do any of this alone. Every account is served by a small team, and you'll work alongside teammates who own the overall strategy and the customer relationship. Your ownership is the content itself: writing much of it, and standing behind all of it.

What You'll Do

• Write high-quality content (blog posts, guides, landing pages, and more) that's genuinely worth reading, grounded in a real understanding of each customer's product and audience

• Write across the full range of campaign formats: thought leadership, blog posts, guides, landing pages, and email nurtures

• Move between registers with ease, from a long-form piece in an executive's voice to tight conversion copy on a landing page

• Review every piece your accounts deliver before it reaches the customer, whether you wrote it, a freelancer wrote it, or it started as an AI-assisted draft. (Note: we have separate Editors who edit pieces in production for feedback. Your role is the final review)

• Turn a campaign plan into a coordinated set of assets that tell one story

• Help manage the freelance writers on your accounts, write briefs they can succeed with, and maintain customer brand guides and other assets for reference.

• Work smoothly with larger marketing teams, keeping quality and momentum through multiple reviewers and longer approval cycles

• Act on customer feedback quickly and thoroughly, and keep track of it, so a customer never has to give the same note twice

• Communicate directly with customers about deliverables, timelines, and revisions, and join customer calls as a trusted voice on the work

• Contribute to performance reporting, helping show customers what shipped, how it's performing, and what we're learning

• Use AI tools thoughtfully, taking advantage of them where they genuinely help, and applying your own judgment and craft where they don't

• Contribute to team knowledge-sharing and internal initiatives, learning from teammates and sharing what you know

What We're Looking For

• 4–6 years of experience in content marketing, with at least 2 of those years in B2B SaaS. Agency experience can be a plus

• Exceptional writing ability: You're first and foremost a writer. You produce publication-ready content with minimal revisions, writing with clarity, precision, and strategic insight, and you adapt your voice to different brands while keeping your standards high

• Campaign thinking: You see how individual pieces of content connect into a larger arc, and you write each one with its place in that arc in mind

• Range as a writer: You're as comfortable with in-depth thought leadership as with concise, conversion-focused copy, and you can switch between them without losing quality

• Strong editorial judgment: You can read someone else's draft, explain clearly why it does or doesn't work. You catch quality problems before customers do

• Experience working with other writers: You've briefed, edited, or managed freelancers or teammates

• Customer communication skills: You're clear, responsive, and trustworthy with customers, and you build confidence through the quality and reliability of your work

• Experience with larger customers: You've worked with enterprise companies or bigger marketing teams, and you handle multiple stakeholders and review rounds with patience and grace

• Strong organizational skills: You can manage multiple accounts, contributors, and deadlines at once without letting quality or dates slip

• AI fluency: You use AI tools to support your workflow responsibly and effectively, you can edit AI-assisted drafts to publication quality, and you stay current on emerging best practices

• Technical curiosity: You genuinely enjoy learning how software products and businesses work so you can write about them with authority

• Ownership and adaptability: You take initiative, navigate ambiguity, and raise problems early, while they're still easy to solve

Room to Grow
Senior Content Marketers at Animalz have real room to grow. You'll start by taking ownership of content for a small set of customers, then take on bigger and more complex accounts as you're ready. From there, many people grow into leading content strategy or managing customer relationships—first alongside a senior teammate, then independently—which is the path to our Associate Head of Content role. Others go deep instead: our most experienced Senior Content Marketers lead content for our most demanding customers and mentor newer teammates, and that's a career here in its own right.
Whichever direction you grow, you'll keep writing. Even our most senior people do; it's the heart of what we sell.

Your First Few Months
You'll spend your first weeks learning our processes and editorial standards and getting to know your accounts, writing your first pieces with plenty of editorial support. Over your first few months, you'll step into full content ownership of your first account (with your Head of Content close by as a backstop) and grow from there at a pace that matches your experience.

Our Values
At Animalz , our values guide how we show up for our customers, our teammates, and the content we create.

• Value Over Vanity: Success isn't measured in customer praise, but in the growth outcomes we deliver for them.

• Two Steps Ahead: Great service means addressing a need or issue before it becomes notable.

• Power Source, Not Power Trip: We find our greatest impact in being in service to others—our customers, our customers' customers, and one another. True power comes not from authority but from influence.

• Pursue Mastery: Through deliberate practice and open collaboration, we build expertise that elevates both our work and our ability to deliver transformative results for our clients.

• Left Brain, Right Brain, Robot Brain: We create extraordinary outcomes by combining empathy and creativity, data and research, and algorithms and AI.

• In the Arena: We don't advise from the sidelines – we're active practitioners who shape the future of our industry through bold experimentation and continuous learning.

Working Arrangements
Location: Fully remote (Americas or EMEA)
Timezone Requirements: At least 4 hours of overlap with US timezones (EST/PST) to collaborate effectively with our team and customers

Compensation & Benefits
Salary Range: $70,000 – $85,000 USD annually
Placement within the range is based on experience, skills, and demonstrated impact in previous content marketing roles.

• Unlimited PTO policy

• Flexible working schedule

• Technology stipend

• Learning stipend

• Health & wellness stipend

• Team lunch stipend

• Health & vision insurance (US only)

• 401(k) retirement plan (US only)

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
At Animalz , we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger. We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities can thrive. We particularly encourage applications from historically underrepresented groups in tech and marketing.

Equal Opportunity
Animalz is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

postings.title: Senior Content Marketer, SEO
postings.descriptionText:
About Animalz

Animalz is a content marketing agency that partners with B2B SaaS companies, venture capital firms, and other tech organizations to drive long-term, sustainable growth through high-quality content.
Our fully remote team of experienced content marketers delivers strategies and content tailored to each customer's goals and context. We pride ourselves on our deep interest and understanding of software products and audiences, our commitment to thought leadership, and our relentless pursuit of mastering our craft.
Our customers include industry leaders like Amplitude, Ramp, and Wistia, as well as high-growth early-stage startups.

About the Role
We're looking for a Senior Content Marketer: an exceptional writer with the editorial judgment to own content quality for the customers they serve.
This is a writing-first role. About 70% of your time will be spent researching and writing content yourself—work that calls for real research, original thinking, and craft.
On the SEO team, that writing is built to perform in search: blog posts, guides, and landing pages that satisfy search intent and still read like something a person wanted to write. Search itself is changing, and this role sits right in the middle of that change. Alongside traditional rankings, you'll help customer content get found and cited by AI search tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's AI Overviews.
The rest of your time goes to making sure everything else your accounts publish is just as good as what you write. You'll manage the freelance writers who contribute to your accounts, keep the content calendar on track, review every piece before it reaches the customer, and ensure customer feedback is acted on and remembered.
You won't do any of this alone. Every account is served by a small team, and you'll work alongside teammates who own the overall strategy and the customer relationship. Your ownership is the content itself: writing much of it, and standing behind all of it.

What You'll Do

• Write high-quality content designed to rank, weaving keyword research, search intent, and on-page best practices into genuinely good writing, grounded in a real understanding of each customer's product and audience

• Review every piece your accounts deliver before it reaches the customer, whether you wrote it, a freelancer wrote it, or it started as an AI-assisted draft. (Note: we have separate Editors who edit pieces in production for feedback. Your role is the final review)

• Refresh and optimize existing content to improve rankings, engagement, and visibility, in both traditional search and AI-powered discovery

• Diagnose why a piece isn't performing, using tools like GA4, Google Search Console, and Ahrefs, and recommend clear, prioritized improvements

• Help manage the freelance writers on your accounts, write briefs they can succeed with, and maintain customer brand guides and other assets for reference.

• Act on customer feedback quickly and thoroughly, and keep track of it, so a customer never has to give the same note twice

• Communicate directly with customers about deliverables, timelines, and revisions, and join customer calls as a trusted voice on the work

• Help improve our AI-assisted content workflows by using them on real work and feeding back what you learn

• Contribute to performance reporting, helping show customers what shipped, how it's performing, and what we're learning

• Use AI tools thoughtfully, taking advantage of them where they genuinely help, and applying your own judgment and craft where they don't

• Contribute to team knowledge-sharing and internal initiatives, learning from teammates and sharing what you know

What We're Looking For

• 4–6 years of experience in content marketing, with at least 2 of those years in B2B SaaS. Agency experience can be a plus

• Exceptional writing ability: You're first and foremost a writer. You produce publication-ready content with minimal revisions, writing with clarity, precision, and strategic insight, and you adapt your voice to different brands while keeping your standards high

• Strong editorial judgment: You can read someone else's draft, explain clearly why it does or doesn't work. You catch quality problems before customers do

• Deep SEO knowledge: You're fluent in keyword research, on-page optimization, content audits, and competitive analysis, and you can diagnose why a piece isn't ranking and what to do about it

• Growing AEO fluency: You understand how AI-driven search is changing content visibility, and you're actively building hands-on skills in making content surface well in AI tools

• Familiarity with SEO and analytics tools such as GA4, Google Search Console, Ahrefs, and Clearscope (or their equivalents)

• Experience working with other writers: You've briefed, edited, or managed freelancers or teammates

• Customer communication skills: You're clear, responsive, and trustworthy with customers, and you build confidence through the quality and reliability of your work

• Strong organizational skills: You can manage multiple accounts, contributors, and deadlines at once without letting quality or dates slip

• AI fluency: You use AI tools to support your workflow responsibly and effectively, you can edit AI-assisted drafts to publication quality, and you stay current on emerging best practices

• Technical curiosity: You genuinely enjoy learning how software products and businesses work so you can write about them with authority

• Ownership and adaptability: You take initiative, navigate ambiguity, and raise problems early, while they're still easy to solve

Room to Grow
Senior Content Marketers at Animalz have real room to grow. You'll start by taking ownership of content for a small set of customers, then take on bigger and more complex accounts as you're ready. From there, many people grow into leading content strategy or managing customer relationships—first alongside a senior teammate, then independently—which is the path to our Associate Head of Content role. Others go deep instead: our most experienced Senior Content Marketers lead content for our most demanding customers and mentor newer teammates, and that's a career here in its own right.
Whichever direction you grow, you'll keep writing. Even our most senior people do; it's the heart of what we sell.

Your First Few Months
You'll spend your first weeks learning our processes and editorial standards and getting to know your accounts, writing your first pieces with plenty of editorial support. Over your first few months, you'll step into full content ownership of your first account (with your Head of Content close by as a backstop) and grow from there at a pace that matches your experience.

Our Values
At Animalz , our values guide how we show up for our customers, our teammates, and the content we create.

• Value Over Vanity: Success isn't measured in customer praise, but in the growth outcomes we deliver for them.

• Two Steps Ahead: Great service means addressing a need or issue before it becomes notable.

• Power Source, Not Power Trip: We find our greatest impact in being in service to others—our customers, our customers' customers, and one another. True power comes not from authority but from influence.

• Pursue Mastery: Through deliberate practice and open collaboration, we build expertise that elevates both our work and our ability to deliver transformative results for our clients.

• Left Brain, Right Brain, Robot Brain: We create extraordinary outcomes by combining empathy and creativity, data and research, and algorithms and AI.

• In the Arena: We don't advise from the sidelines – we're active practitioners who shape the future of our industry through bold experimentation and continuous learning.

Working Arrangements
Location: Fully remote (Americas or EMEA)
Timezone Requirements: At least 4 hours of overlap with US timezones (EST/PST) to collaborate effectively with our team and customers

Compensation & Benefits
Salary Range: $70,000 – $85,000 USD annually
Placement within the range is based on experience, skills, and demonstrated impact in previous content marketing roles.

• Unlimited PTO policy

• Flexible working schedule

• Technology stipend

• Learning stipend

• Health & wellness stipend

• Team lunch stipend

• Health & vision insurance (US only)

• 401(k) retirement plan (US only)

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
At Animalz , we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger. We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities can thrive. We particularly encourage applications from historically underrepresented groups in tech and marketing.

Equal Opportunity
Animalz is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

About AirDNA

We built AirDNA to solve a problem: how do you make smart short-term rental decisions when there’s too much guesswork and not enough good data? What started in a garage in California in 2015 is now a global team helping thousands of people — from aspiring hosts to major real estate firms — make confident choices about where to invest, what to charge, and how to grow. Our mission is simple: give people the tools they need to build freedom through short-term rentals. Whether that means buying their first Airbnb or scaling a portfolio, we’re here to help unlock financial independence and growth. We track 10M+ listings in 120,000 markets, and our platform is trusted by users in over 100 countries. It’s big data, made useful.

The AirDNA team
We’re a curious, driven, and kind group of humans who genuinely love what we do. Our values — Happy, Hungry, Honest — guide how we show up for our customers and for each other. You’ll get a feel once you meet us.
We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage you to apply even if you don’t check every box. Passion, potential, and perspective matter here.

The Role
We’re looking for a Strategy & Planning (S&P) Analyst who sits at the intersection of strategy and data . Partnering closely with the S&P Manager, CFO, and CEO, you’ll help leadership answer the company’s most important business questions, and you’ll build the data foundation that makes those answers possible.
On the strategy side , you’ll dig into what’s driving performance, uncover opportunities and risks, and turn your analysis into clear recommendations that shape executive decisions. On the data side, you’ll audit, consolidate, and enrich AirDNA ’s core data across Growth, Finance, Marketing, and Customer Support to create a single source of truth for the business.
This is a great opportunity to shape both how AirDNA sees its data and what it does with it . We’re looking for a hands-on who takes initiative, brings their own ideas, and owns projects from the first question to the final recommendation.

Here's what you'll get to do:

Strategy & Insights

• Partner directly with the CFO and CEO on high-impact strategic questions, turning complex analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

• Proactively identify trends, risks, and growth opportunities across the business, including questions leadership hasn’t asked yet.

• Support planning, forecasting, and performance reviews, helping leadership understand what’s working, what isn’t, and why.

• Lead your own strategic initiatives end to end, from scoping the problem to presenting the recommendation and following it through.

• Partner cross-functionally with Growth, Finance, Marketing, and Customer Support to align on KPI priorities and close data gaps.

Data Foundation

• Audit and map existing data tables across Finance, Growth, Marketing, and Customer Support.

• Design and build a unified master table architecture that consolidates cross-functional data into a single source of truth.

• Create executive dashboards in Sigma or similar BI tools that surface real-time KPIs for leadership.

Here's what you'll need to be successful:

• 2+ years of experience in a data-driven, analytical role (e.g., strategy, BizOps, FP&A, consulting, or business intelligence).

• Strong SQL proficiency (complex queries, joins, window functions, CTEs) across databases like Snowflake, PostgreSQL, or Redshift.

•
Strategic mindset: you care as much about what the data means and what we should do about it as about how to query it.

•
Initiative and ownership: you don’t wait to be told what to analyze. You form a point of view, bring ideas, and drive your own projects forward.

•
Executive communication: you can translate complex analysis into a clear story and recommendation for leadership and non-technical stakeholders.

• Experience using Hex, Sigma, Power BI, or similar. Advanced Excel/Sheets skills are a given.

• Collaborative and low-ego: you build trust quickly and thrive working cross-functionally.

• Accountable and adaptable: you meet deadlines and reprioritize fast in a high-growth environment.

• Hungry to grow: coachable, curious, and excited to scale AirDNA through better insights.

•
Bonus points: familiarity with ETL tools (dbt, Airflow, Fivetran), AI tooling (Claude, Zapier), or experience with Amplitude, Stripe, or HubSpot.

Here's what you can expect from us:

• Unlimited vacation policy; take time when you need it

• Continuing education stipend

• Paid parental leave

•
Real influence: your analysis will directly shape decisions made by our CFO and CEO.

•
A seat at the strategy table: high visibility with leadership, with room to grow your scope as the S&P function grows.

•
Build something from scratch: design how AirDNA measures and understands its business.

•
World-class data: work with one of the richest short-term rental datasets in the world.

• A culture that rewards initiative, curiosity, and a Get Stuff Done mentality.

Hiring process

Location: Remote, Latin America (LATAM)
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote

Openings: 1
Industry: Real Estate Finance / Private Lending
Compensation: $1,300 to $1,800 USD/month

Schedule: Monday to Friday | 8:45 AM to 5:45 PM U.S. Eastern Time (ET)
English Proficiency: Advanced written and spoken English required
Start Date: As soon as possible (early November 2026)

About the Company
Our client is a U.S.-based private real estate lender that provides short-term, business-purpose loans to real estate investors.
The company finances Fix & Flip, Bridge, DSCR rental and Ground-Up Construction projects and works with a third-party loan servicer, note buyers and capital partners to manage its loan portfolio.
As its portfolio grows, the company is building out its remote operations team to keep every funded loan accurately tracked and every borrower well supported.

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Loan Servicing Specialist to own the post-closing servicing workflow and borrower and partner follow-through.
You will board funded loans with the third-party servicer, manage construction draws, monitor maturities, payments and delinquencies, and answer borrower and partner questions until each one is resolved.
The third-party servicer prepares servicing calculations; this specialist reviews and coordinates them. Speed, accuracy, ownership and exceptional borrower service are central to the role.

What You'll Do

Loan Boarding & Records

• Board funded loans with the third-party servicer.

• Validate terms, balances, reserves and maturity dates.

• Maintain accurate records in the company's loan portal and servicing systems.

Construction Draws

• Manage construction draw requests end to end: budget and reserve checks, inspections, documentation, review and approvals within delegated limits.

• Coordinate disbursements and give borrowers proactive updates.

Maturities, Extensions & Payoffs

• Monitor upcoming maturities and coordinate extensions.

• Coordinate payoffs and extensions with the servicer, reviewing its calculations, statements and documents for accuracy.

• Track completion and lien releases.

Portfolio Monitoring

• Identify inactive or stalled loans with no recent progress, updates or borrower communication.

• Contact the relevant parties, document status and escalate risks.

• Monitor missed payments and delinquencies, follow up with borrowers and the servicer, and escalate potential defaults or unresolved issues.

Borrower & Partner Support

• Answer borrower, note buyer and warehouse lender questions about loans, draws, balances, payments, extensions and payoffs.

• Own each inquiry until it is resolved.

Qualifications

Required

• At least 1.5 years of hands-on experience at a U.S. hard money or private real estate lender, originating or servicing business-purpose investment property loans (Fix & Flip, Bridge, DSCR and/or Ground-Up Construction).

• Direct experience servicing short-term hard money or business-purpose loans.

• Experience with construction draw management, payoffs and extensions.

• Advanced written and spoken English.

• High attention to detail.

• Ability to work in Gmail, GoHighLevel (GHL) or a similar CRM, and an online loan portal for documents, files and workflow.

• Hardworking, dependable, proactive and accountable. You take ownership and follow up without reminders.

• Comfortable in a fast-paced lending business, handling urgent requests and meeting deadlines without compromising accuracy or controls.

• Availability to work 8:45 AM to 5:45 PM U.S. Eastern Time.

Preferred

• Experience working with a third-party loan servicer.

Please note: conventional consumer mortgage experience alone (FHA, VA, Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac loans) does not meet the experience requirement.

How Success Is Measured

• Funded loans are boarded quickly and accurately.

• Draw requests are processed on time and within approved budgets.

• Maturities, extensions and payoffs are handled before deadlines.

• Stalled loans, missed payments and potential defaults are flagged early.

• Borrower and partner questions get fast, accurate answers.

Why Join Us?

•
Fully Remote Opportunity: Work from anywhere in Latin America with a U.S.-based lender.

•
Competitive Compensation: Earn $1,300 to $1,800 USD per month.

•
Meaningful Responsibility: Own the health of a growing loan portfolio.

•
Professional Growth: Build deeper experience in U.S. private real estate lending and servicing.

Important Notes

• Candidates must reside in Latin America.

• Direct experience servicing hard money or business-purpose loans is required.

• Availability to work U.S. Eastern Time business hours is required.

• Excellent English communication skills are essential.

• Please submit your CV in English and include the lender(s) you worked for, your dates of employment and the loan types you handled.

This is a remote/telecommute position.

• Feed what you learn on the ground back to marketing and sales leadership

Campaigns & Lifecycle

• Test and optimize to lift conversion, repeat, and cross-brand rates

CRM, Reporting & Analytics

• Build self-serve dashboards and automated alerts covering application health, application-to-order conversion, and tier movement

• Surface leading indicators like primed leads, idle accounts, stalled deals, and tier gaps

• Deliver clear recommendations on book structure, engagement volume, sales activities, and deal management

CX & Supply Chain Partnership

• Act as the single point of contact for trade across CX and Supply Chain

• Define escalation steps and expected response times

• Find and unblock stuck orders before delivery friction costs us accounts we have already won

Qualifications

• Proven experience working remotely with U.S.-based teams

• Strong English communication skills, written and verbal

• Strong analytical skills, including building funnel reporting and turning findings into a prioritized plan of action

• Experience driving a sales team to a number without managing it directly

• We are building with AI as part of how we work. We are looking for people who are curious about AI-assisted tools and eager to adopt them.

Space Inch is looking for an Engineering Engagement Lead to look after our engineers within a long-standing partnership with one of the largest investment managers in the U.S, who is a S&P 500 company . Our engineers work embedded in the client’s teams, and the client directs their day-to-day work. Your job is everything around that work: making sure each engineer meets Space Inch ’s standards, understanding what they’re building and why it matters to the client’s business, helping them grow, and keeping communication clear between our people and the client.
This is a people, communication, and account role , which means that you won’t assign tasks, run sprints, or make architecture decisions. An engineering background is a preference, but it’s not a disqualifying criteria. What really matters is an engineer’s mindset : you can sit down with an engineer or a client’s engineering manager, understand what’s being built, and have a real conversation about it.

Our mission, vision, and values
At Space Inch , we prioritize alignment with our clients and team, ensuring a deep understanding of their needs. We are committed to delivering exceptional work while supporting the personal and professional growth of our team members.

Working at Space Inch

• Our remote-first team of around 80+ people is based across the EU (mostly Croatia), the US, and Latin America, with a growing presence in Brazil.

• Occasional travel for client visits and company retreats.

• This role is embedded within a single long-standing client partnership, though you'll draw on Space Inch 's broader engineering community and practices.

• We support work/life balance for our team.

Requirements

•
Experience : 10+ years in engineering and people leadership, engagement or account management, or technical project/product management in an agency, consultancy, nearshore, or client-embedded environment; preferably coming from an engineering background, but not a must.

•
An engineer’s mindset : you understand modern software development (SDLC, common architectures and stacks) well enough to follow what engineers are building, hold your own with client engineering and product managers, and notice when something is off. You don’t need to write code.

•
Real curiosity about the client’s business : you invest the time to learn the domain, why each application matters, and what workflow it replaces, so client stakeholders see you as someone who adds value.

•
A clear system for evaluating people : you can explain how you know someone is doing a great job, using standards, evidence, and feedback from several sources, and how you turn that into specific, actionable coaching.

•
Exceptional communicator and mediator who handles sensitive topics (compensation, retention, disengagement, underperformance) directly and with care, across written, async, live, and cross-cultural communication.

• Proven track record of growing engineers : you’ve guided engineers along their career paths, from junior to senior and from individual contributor toward leadership, built development plans that led to real promotions, and can point to people who grew under your leadership.

•
Experience managing senior client stakeholders : gathering honest feedback, managing expectations, and showing the value our people bring.

•
Practical fluency with AI as a working tool : you can assess whether engineers are using AI well against defined practices and push them to improve.

• Experience leading distributed or remote people, including those who work mostly on their own.

Key responsibilities

•
Evaluation against our standards : Regularly assess every engineer and project against Space Inch ’s project success standards, and whether we’re meeting both the client’s needs and our team members’ needs.

•
Client feedback loop : Work with the client’s engineering and product managers to gather feedback on each engineer, including quality of work, taking into account how each client team operates.

•
Coaching and growth : Run regular 1:1s, give candid feedback, and build development plans that help engineers level up. Work with Engineering Leads, who coach informally, to round out evaluations.

•
Retention and connection : Keep engineers engaged and connected to Space Inch , especially those working alone on client projects. Spot retention risks early and resolve them.

•
Coaching and career growth : Run regular 1:1s, give candid feedback, and build development plans tied to Space Inch ’s career paths. Identify engineers who are ready for the next level, build their promotion cases, and support those moving toward leadership roles. Work with Engineering Leads, who coach informally, to round out evaluations.

•
Account management : Act as Space Inch ’s senior point of contact with the client on how our people are doing; manage expectations and help tell the story of the impact of our work.

•
Facilitating communication : Help engineers navigate shifting priorities, unclear ownership, and unrealistic timelines, and bridge communication gaps between our team and the client.

•
AI practice : Check that engineers follow the AI practices we define, help them improve, and share what works across the team.

Typical challenges you’ll be solving

• Understanding a wide range of client applications well enough that client managers take your input seriously.

• Keeping engineers who work individually within client teams motivated and connected to Space Inch .

• Helping engineers handle a fast-changing client environment: shifting priorities, unclear ownership, and tight deadlines.

• Growing engineers’ careers when the client directs their daily work, and making their progress visible enough to support promotions.

• Turning feedback from engineers, Engineering Leads, and client managers into fair, specific evaluations and coaching.

• Raising the bar on how the team uses AI, measured by outcomes rather than adoption for its own sake.

Qualities for success

• Strong people instincts: engineers trust your guidance, feel supported in 1:1s, and are honest with you about what isn’t working.

• Adapts communication style across coaching, difficult conversations, and client discussions.

• A systems thinker who builds repeatable ways to evaluate and grow people, and spots broken communication loops before they escalate.

• Comfortable making decisions and owning the outcome, even when the first attempt fails.

• Calm under client pressure, and doesn’t pass that pressure to the team.

The role is right for you if

• You lead through trust, conversation, and presence, and you enjoy helping people get better at what they do.

• You like learning how a business works and connecting people’s work to what the client actually needs.

• You enjoy building a clear system for evaluating and developing people, and refining it over time.

• You find it rewarding when someone you’ve coached takes the next step in their career.

• You’re comfortable in a setup where the client directs the day-to-day work and your impact comes through people and relationships.

The role is not right for you if

• You want to run delivery, assign work, or own a product roadmap.

• You want a primarily hands-on engineering role.

• You aren’t interested in learning the client’s business in depth.

• You’d rather wait for direction than propose a way forward.

What’s in it for you

postings.title: Product Designer (Intl. - Full-time)
postings.descriptionText:
Spate is a trend intelligence platform for consumer brands in beauty, wellness, and food and beverage. We analyze anonymous, aggregated public consumer data to spot emerging trends early and explain why they're growing, so brands can make product and marketing decisions with confidence.
Our founders, Yarden Horwitz and Olivier Zimmer, started Google's Trendspotting division and called trends like turmeric, cold brew, and face masks before they went mainstream. Spate is Y Combinator-backed, and more than 200 brands use it, including Sephora, L'Oréal Paris, Estée Lauder Companies, Unilever, P&G, and e.l.f. Our data regularly appears in The New York Times, WWD, British Vogue, and The Business of Fashion.

About the role
We're hiring our first dedicated product designer, full-time, to shape Spate's core product: the dashboard where brand teams explore trends, build reports, and work with our AI assistant.
Our platform will change a lot over the next year or two as we rebuild around LLM-powered features. We already ship an AI Assistant, AI Reports (an LLM-powered dashboard builder), and in-dashboard summaries and analysis. We need someone who can work out what those experiences should be, not just how they should look.
Our users are brand innovation teams, product marketers, social media teams, and agencies. Most aren't data analysts, so much of the job is turning dense trend data into something clear and actionable.
You'll join the Frontend & UX team, four people including you, and report to our frontend lead. The role is fully remote, and we're hiring in the UK, central Europe, and Latin America, where many of our team already work. You’ll need to be based between US Central Time (UTC−6) and Central European Time (UTC+1). We require you to be available for core collaboration hours of 9:00 AM–12:00 PM Eastern (2:00–5:00 PM UK, 3:00–6:00 PM CET or your local equivalent).
This is a remote, Full-time employee position.

What you'll own
The product, not just the screens. At Spate, product design and UI/UX design happen together. Features aren't fully defined and then handed to a designer. You'll help decide what we build and why, and stay involved from the first conversation to launch. You'll work with our frontend lead to choose the right deliverable for each problem: a written proposal, a user flow, a prototype, or a full Figma spec.
Finding problems worth solving. Find user pain points on your own, through customer calls, interviews, feedback, and usage data. Then take them from problem to proposal: frame the problem, explore options, and make the case for a direction. Leadership sets the overall direction and can help point you at problems, but you won't need our input to get started.
How our AI features work. Decide when something should be a chat, a report, or an inline summary. Define how we show where an insight came from, and how we handle loading, uncertainty, and wrong answers. Help shape the voice and structure of AI-generated insights, because in an LLM product the words are part of the UX.
The design system. We have a Figma library and a React component library that are only loosely in sync. You'll own the system's principles and the Figma side, and partner with our frontend engineers to make the two a single source of truth. The goal is that everyday design decisions are answered by the system, so engineers can ship UI that feels like Spate without waiting on design. This includes data visualization standards and patterns for AI features.
The feedback loop, with our frontend lead. Co-own product metrics, user feedback tracking, and quality evaluation for our LLM features. A big part of this is defining what a good AI answer looks like for our users, and turning that into rubrics we can measure.

Requirements

What we're looking for
We care more about mindset than years of experience. You're driven, you care about making a good product, and you have a growth mindset. You value autonomy and self-direction.

• 3+ years of product design experience, ideally owning features end to end in a B2B or SaaS product.

• Strong product opinions. You think about what to build and why, not just how it looks, and you're comfortable defending and revising your ideas.

• A portfolio that shows how you framed problems, not just how you solved them. At least one case study should start from a fuzzy problem with no spec.

• Experience designing data-heavy products such as dashboards, analytics, or reporting tools.

• You've worked within or contributed to a design system, and understand how components and patterns scale.

• Real curiosity about AI products, ideally with some hands-on exploration.

• Strong written communication in English. We're remote, so your proposals and decisions need to stand on their own.

• Fluent in Figma, with AI tools in your everyday workflow.

Nice to have

• Experience as the first or only designer on a team.

• You've built or substantially evolved a design system that engineers adopted.

• Experience designing AI features, or writing evaluation rubrics for LLM output.

• Depth in data visualization.

• Familiarity with consumer goods, beauty, food, or marketing and insights tools.

• Comfort building quick functional prototypes with AI tools to test ideas against real outputs.

Your first 90 days

• First 30 days: Learn the product and the people who use it. Review customer calls, feedback and usage data, and audit the Figma library against our React components. Ship one small, real improvement.

• By day 60: Publish a map of our users' top pain points and goals. Take one meaningful feature from pain point to agreed proposal, with prototypes.

• By day 90: Have the design system's first principles documented and in use. Start co-owning metrics, feedback tracking, and LLM evals with our frontend lead.

How we work
Contributors at Spate work flexibly, with few meetings, a lot of impact, and real say over the direction of their work. Leadership sets product direction and priorities, and you shape how we get there. That means bringing proposals rather than waiting for briefs.
This isn't the right place if you need every decision approved or every project precisely spec'd before you start.

You will be the primary owner of long-lead equipment strategy, from early project scoping through delivery, installation, and commissioning, working within our Owner Furnished, Contractor Installed (OFCI) procurement model.

Supplier Management and Sourcing

• Identify, qualify, and manage strategic suppliers for long-lead equipment, including OEMs and key component manufacturers.

- Develop supplier scorecards and conduct regular business reviews to drive performance, reliability, and continuous improvement.

• Own the full purchase-to-delivery lifecycle for long-lead equipment, ensuring on-time delivery to project sites and facilities.
- Coordinate closely with Logistics, Site Operations, and Installation teams on shipping plans, customs requirements, staging, and sequencing.
- Proactively monitor and manage purchase orders, exceptions, and changes, resolving issues before they impact project timelines.

Risk Management and Mitigation

• Identify supply, schedule, quality, and capacity risks for long-lead items and develop mitigation plans, including alternate sources, safety stock, and dual-sourcing strategies.
- Maintain and regularly update a risk register for critical equipment and components.
- Escalate and resolve critical issues with suppliers and internal stakeholders, ensuring clear communication and decision-making.

Process Improvement and Systems

• Define and refine the processes, tools, and KPIs used to manage long-lead equipment across the organization.
- Partner with IT and Systems teams to improve ERP/MRP, procurement, and tracking workflows for long-lead items.
- Drive standardization of BOM structures, lead-time assumptions, and planning parameters to improve data quality and planning accuracy.

Cross-Functional Leadership

• Act as the primary point of contact for long-lead equipment topics across Project Management, Engineering, Construction, and Operations.
- Lead cross-functional reviews to align on equipment priorities, trade-offs, and decisions.
- Mentor and support junior supply chain and procurement team members.

About You

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
- Experience in supply chain, procurement, or operations, with significant responsibility for long-lead materials or capital equipment.
- Proven track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects with tight deadlines and high business impact.
- Strong experience with ERP/MRP systems and advanced planning tools.
- Excellent negotiation, contract management, and supplier relationship skills.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data and translate it into clear actions and recommendations.
- Effective communicator, able to influence at multiple levels and work cross-functionally in a fast-paced environment.

Nice to Have

• Experience with complex capital projects in data centres, energy, construction, semiconductors, or advanced manufacturing.
- Background managing global supplier bases and international logistics.
- Experience implementing or improving long-lead planning processes and tools at scale.

Why this role matters
Long-lead equipment is often the critical path for bringing new AI capacity online. In this role, your work directly shapes how quickly and reliably Nscale can deliver infrastructure to customers. Success will be measured by:
- On-time delivery performance for long-lead equipment.
- Schedule adherence for critical project milestones that depend on long-lead items.
- Supplier performance across quality, lead time, and responsiveness.
- Forecast accuracy and a measurable reduction in supply-related schedule risk.

What We Can Offer You

• Highly competitive package, including base salary and equity, with reviews every 12 months.
- Join one of the fastest-growing tech startups: your chance to push boundaries, collaborate with brilliant minds, and make your mark on cutting-edge AI.

postings.descriptionText:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs.
